newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen off $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were seen dipping another $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt on Thursday, pressured by large hog supplies and lower bids by packers still struggling with poor operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen ranging from $57.00 to $57.50 and Illinois top prices could span $56.00 to $56.50, sources in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top values for hogs shipped to the plant were seen at $56.50 to $57.00, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts on Tuesday tallied 113,000 head, above the 110,000 estimate, USDA said. Wednesday's estimate was 105,000 head versus 95,000 a week ago.

Price weakness also was tied to news John Morrell and Co. was suspending second shift operations at its Sioux Falls, S.D. plant for a week starting Monday because of poor margins, cash market sources said. The plant has a daily slaughter capacity of 15,000 head, but has been running below capacity since early May due to the unprofitable margins, market sources said.
The news about Morrell, a unit of Smithfield Foods, was the latest in a series of disclosures by prominent pork packing companies about cutbacks in production due to unprofitable market conditions.
